title.bestPracticeDefinition: Full title by which the Dataset is known.

subtitle.bestPracticeDefinition:
A secondary title used to amplify or state certain limitations on the main title.
Tip: The subtitle is not included in the auto-generated citation. If you want the subtitle to be included in the citation, then you must add itto the Title field in addition to the Subtitle field.the Subtitle field.

alternativeTitle.bestPracticeDefinition: A title by which the work is commonly referred, or an abbreviation of the title.Tip: Acronym, short form, or translation of full title.

alternativeURL.bestPracticeDefinition: A URL where the dataset can be viewed, such as a personal or project website.

otherIdAgency.bestPracticeDefinition: Name of agency which generated this identifier.
otherIdAgency.example: Youth Communication Development Project, Education Department, Queen's University

otherIdValue.bestPracticeDefinition: Another unique identifier that identifies this Dataset (e.g., producer's or another repository's number).

authorName.bestPracticeDefinition: The author's Family Name, Given Name or the name of the organizatfion responsible for this Dataset.

authorAffiliation.bestPracticeDefinition:
The organization with which the author is affiliated.
Tip: Use the full official name of the organization; avoid abbreviations.

authorIdentifierScheme.bestPracticeDefinition:
Name of the identifier scheme (ORCID, ISNI).
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select one.

authorIdentifier.bestPracticeDefinition: Uniquely identifies an individual author or organization, according to various schemes.

datasetContactName.bestPracticeDefinition: The contact's Family Name, Given Name or the name of the organization.

datasetContactAffiliation.bestPracticeDefinition:
The organization with which the contact is affiliated.
Tip: use the full official name of the organization; avoid abbreviations.

datasetContactEmail.bestPracticeDefinition: The e-mail address(es) of the contact(s) for the Dataset. This will not be displayed.

dsDescriptionValue.bestPracticeDefinition: A summary describing the purpose, nature, and scope of the Dataset.Tip: A good description will identify the content of the dataset and help a user determine if they have the technical ability to use it.
dsDescriptionValue.example: The Social Media Use Among Teens survey was conducted by the Youth Communication Development Project to understand social media communication behaviours among youth in Canada. The survey collected responses from Canadian youth using an online questionnaire that asks about social media use including, platform type, frequency of use, activity type, and location of use. This information is supplemented with the respondent’s demographic and household characteristics

dsDescriptionDate.bestPracticeDefinition: In cases where a Dataset contains more than one description (for example, one might be supplied by the data producer and another prepared by the data repository where the data are deposited), the date attribute is used to distinguish between the two descriptions. The date attribute follows the ISO convention of YYYY-MM-DD.

subject.bestPracticeDefinition:
Domain-specific Subject Categories that are topically relevant to the Dataset.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply.Tip: Select one or more Subject terms to represent the broad domain or domains the dataset relates to.

keywordValue.bestPracticeDefinition:
Key terms that describe important aspects of the Dataset. Can be used for building keyword indexes and for classification and retrieval purposes. A controlled vocabulary can be employed. The vocab attribute is provided for specification of the controlled vocabulary in use, such as LCSH, MeSH, or others. The vocabURI attribute specifies the location for the full controlled vocabulary.
Tip: The Keyword field is repeatable. Put each keyword in its own field by pressing the “+” button.Tip: In Dataverse metadata, keywords are case sensitive. Use sentence case for free text terms (i.e., capitalize the first word and proper nouns).
Tip: Use free-text terms or terms from a controlled vocabulary in this field to represent specific or granular topics associated with the dataset. Think of them like tags.
Tip: FASTand RVMFASTare  good, general-purpose controlled vocabularies adapted from Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH).Tip: Geographic place names should be entered in the Geospatial metadata section.

keywordVocabulary.bestPracticeDefinition:
For the specification of the keyword controlled vocabulary in use, such as LCSH, MeSH, or others.
Tip: Use this field when the Keyword term is from a controlled vocabulary
keywordVocabulary.example: Government of Canada Core Subject Thesaurus

keywordVocabularyURI.bestPracticeDefinition:
Keyword vocabulary URL points to the web presence that describes the keyword vocabulary, if appropriate. Enter an absolute URL where the keyword vocabulary web site is found, such as http://www.my.org.
Tip: Use this field when the Keyword term is from a controlled vocabulary.

topicClassValue.bestPracticeDefinition:
Topic or Subject term that is relevant to this Dataset.
Tip: The Keyword field is repeatable. Put each keyword in its own field by pressing the “+” button.
Tip: In Dataversemetadata, keywords are case sensitive. Use sentence case for free text terms (i.e., capitalize the first word and proper nouns).
Tip: Use free-text terms or terms from a controlled vocabulary in this field to represent specific or granular topics associated with thedataset. Think of them like tags.
Tip: FASTand RVMFASTare good, general-purpose controlled vocabularies adapted from Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH).
Tip: Geographic place names should be entered in the Geospatial metadata section.

topicClassVocab.bestPracticeDefinition:
Provided for specification of the controlled vocabulary in use, e.g., LCSH, MeSH, etc.
Tip: Use this field when the Topic Classification term is from a controlled vocabulary
topicClassVocab.example: Government of Canada Core Subject Thesaurus

topicClassVocabURI.bestPracticeDefinition:
Specifies the URL location for the full controlled vocabulary.
Tip: Use this field when the Topic Classification term is from a controlled vocabulary.

publicationCitation.bestPracticeDefinition: The full bibliographic citation for this related publication.
publicationCitation.example: Doe, Jane. (2017). Teen use of social media: analysis of self-reported communication behaviours. Journal of Social Media Use. Vol 1. Iss. 1, 2017.

publicationIDType.bestPracticeDefinition:
The type of digital identifier used for this publication (e.g., Digital Object Identifier (DOI)).
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select one.
Tip: Use a persistentidentifier where possible (e.g.,DOI, handle, ISBN). If only a URL is available, select the type “url” and enter the URL into both the ID Number and URL fields.

publicationIDNumber.bestPracticeDefinition:
The identifier for the selected ID type.
Tip:If using ID Type “url”, enter the URL into both this field and the URL field.

publicationURL.bestPracticeDefinition:
Link to the publication web page (e.g., journal article page, archive record page, or other).
Tip: This field is only used for display purposes in the Dataverseinterface. For interoperability, ensure that the ID Type and ID Number fields are also completed.

notesText.bestPracticeDefinition: Additional important information about the Dataset.
notesText.example: This survey was administered online. Mode of interview has been found to impact results,therefore it is not recommended that these results are compared with other survey results where the interview mode was telephone based.

language.bestPracticeDefinition:
Language of the Dataset.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply.

producerAffiliation.bestPracticeDefinition: The organization with which the producer is affiliated.

producerAbbreviation.bestPracticeDefinition: The abbreviation by which the producer is commonly known. (ex. IQSS, ICPSR)

producerURL.bestPracticeDefinition: Producer URL points to the producer's web presence, if appropriate. Enter an absolute URL where the producer's web site is found, such as http://www.my.org.

producerLogoURL.bestPracticeDefinition: URL for the producer's logo, which points to this producer's web-accessible logo image. Enter an absolute URL where the producer's logo image is found, such as http://www.my.org/images/logo.gif.

productionDate.bestPracticeDefinition:
Date when the data collection or other materials were produced (not distributed, published or archived).
Tip: Date when dataset was finalized and ready for analysis or distribution.

productionPlace.bestPracticeDefinition:
The location where the data collection and any other related materials were produced.
Tip: Include an institution if relevant. Avoid abbreviations.

contributorType.bestPracticeDefinition: The type of contributor of theresource.Note: This field is a drop-down list; select one.

contributorName.bestPracticeDefinition: The Family Name, Given Name or organization name of the contributor

grantNumberAgency.bestPracticeDefinition: Name of agency which generated this identifier.
grantNumberAgency.example: Youth Communication Development Project, Education Department, Queen's University

grantNumberValue.bestPracticeDefinition: The grant or contract number of the project that sponsored the effort.

distributorAffiliation.bestPracticeDefinition: The organization with which the distributor contact is affiliated.

distributorAbbreviation.bestPracticeDefinition: The abbreviation by which this distributor is commonly known (e.g., IQSS, ICPSR).

distributorURL.bestPracticeDefinition: Distributor URL points to the distributor's web presence, if appropriate. Enter an absolute URL where the distributor's web site is found, such as http://www.my.org.

distributorLogoURL.bestPracticeDefinition: URL of the distributor's logo, which points to this distributor's web-accessible logo image. Enter an absolute URL where the distributor's logo image is found, such as http://www.my.org/images/logo.gif.

distributionDate.bestPracticeDefinition:
Date that the work was made available for distribution/presentation.
Tip: This field may be the same as the Deposit Date. Use Distribution Date only if data was previously distributed.

depositor.bestPracticeDefinition:
The person (Family Name, Given Name) or the name of the organization that deposited this Dataset to the repository.
Tip: The name of the person/institution who provided the dataset(s) to the archive (i.e., not necessarily the person preparing theDataverse repository submission

dateOfDeposit.bestPracticeDefinition:
Date that the Dataset was deposited into the repository.
Tip: Deposit Date is pre-populated with the date of upload to the Dataverse repository.  It can be edited to reflect the date when the data was received by an external or mediated data repository service.

timePeriodCoveredStart.bestPracticeDefinition: Start date which reflects the time period covered by the data, not the dates of coding or making documents machine-readable or the dates the data were collected.

timePeriodCoveredEnd.bestPracticeDefinition: End date which reflects the time period covered by the data, not the dates of coding or making documents machine-readable or the dates the data were collected.

dateOfCollectionStart.bestPracticeDefinition: Date when the data collection started.

dateOfCollectionEnd.bestPracticeDefinition: Date when the data collection ended.

kindOfData.bestPracticeDefinition: Type of data included in the file: survey data, census/enumeration data, aggregate data, clinical data, event/transaction data, program source code, machine-readable text, administrative records data, experimental data, psychological test, textual data, coded textual, coded documents, time budget diaries, observation data/ratings, process-produced data, or other.

seriesName.bestPracticeDefinition: Name of the dataset series to which the Dataset belongs.

seriesInformation.bestPracticeDefinition: History of the series and summary of those features that apply to the series as a whole.
seriesInformation.example: Established in 2005, the Youth Communication Development Project aims to gather key research and data about youth development and social media use through a series of independent, annual, cross-sectional surveys titled Social Media Use Among Teens. The overall objective of the program is to gather data on youth and social media trends in order to monitor changes in the well-being of young Canadians, and to provide information on specific social policy issues.

softwareName.bestPracticeDefinition:
Name of software used to generate the Dataset.
Tip: Useful for specialized software or instruments.

softwareVersion.bestPracticeDefinition: Version of the software used to generate the Dataset.

relatedMaterial.bestPracticeDefinition:
Any material related to this Dataset.
Tip: This is secondary materials in relation to the study description, such as technical documentation or a website detailing more information about the study.
relatedMaterial.example: Youth Social Media Trends: 2015 Report [Canada]. YCDP, Queen's University, 2016. Access URL: http://dataverse.scholarsportal.info/queensu/2016report.pdf

relatedDatasets.bestPracticeDefinition:
Any Datasets that are related to this Dataset, such as previous research on this subject.
Tip: This would include previous versions of the data (rounds or waves) or other collections generated by the same data.
relatedDatasets.example: Social Media Use Among Teens, 2010 [Canada]. YCDP, Queen's University, 2011. DOI. Access URL: http://dataverse.scholarsportal.info/queensu/2010data.xhtml

otherReferences.bestPracticeDefinition:
Any references that would serve as background or supporting material to this Dataset.
Tip: This includes documentation such as codebooks, questionnaires, methodology, coding files, etc.
otherReferences.example: Social Media Use Among Teens: Survey Questionnaire, 2015 [Canada]. YCDP, Queen's University, 2016. DOI. Access URL: http://dataverse.scholarsportal.info/queensu/2016questionnaire.pdf

dataSources.bestPracticeDefinition: List of books, articles, serials, or machine-readable data files that served as the sources of the data collection.
dataSources.example: Statistics Canada. National Household Survey, 2011: Median Household Income by Census Tracts, Census Metropolitan Areas. NHS 2011, Statistics Canada. Access URL: https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/nhs-enm/2011/dp-pd/prof/index.cfm?Lang=E

originOfSources.bestPracticeDefinition: For historical materials, information about the origin of the sources and the rules followed in establishing the sources should be specified.

characteristicOfSources.bestPracticeDefinition:
Assessment of characteristics and source material.
Tip: Describes noteworthy aspects of the data collected.

accessToSources.bestPracticeDefinition:
Level of documentation of the original sources.
Tip: May be used to explain any restrictions or access to source data documentation.

country.bestPracticeDefinition: The country or nation that the Dataset is about.

state.bestPracticeDefinition: The state or province that the Dataset is about. Use GeoNames for correct spelling and avoid abbreviations.

city.bestPracticeDefinition: The name of the city that the Dataset is about. Use GeoNames for correct spelling and avoid abbreviations.

otherGeographicCoverage.bestPracticeDefinition: Other information on the geographic coverage of the data.

geographicUnit.bestPracticeDefinition: Lowest level of geographic aggregation covered by the Dataset, e.g., village, county, region.

westLongitude.bestPracticeDefinition: Westernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -180.0 <= West  Bounding Longitude Value <= 180.0.

eastLongitude.bestPracticeDefinition: Easternmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -180.0 <= East Bounding Longitude Value <= 180.0.

northLatitude.bestPracticeDefinition: Northernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -90.0 <= North Bounding Latitude Value <= 90.0.

southLatitude.bestPracticeDefinition: Southernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -90.0 <= South Bounding Latitude Value <= 90.0.

geographicReferenceDateType.example: revision, expiry, lastUpdate, lastRevision, nextUpdate, unavailable, inForce, adopted, deprecated, superseded, publication

geometricObjectType.example: curve, composite, complex, point, solid, or surface

geographicDimensionNameType.example: row, column, vertical, track, crossTrack, line, sample, or time

unitOfAnalysis.bestPracticeDefinition: Basic unit of analysis or observation that this Dataset describes, such as individuals, families/households, groups, institutions/organizations, administrative units, and more. For information about the DDI's controlled vocabulary for this element, please refer to the DDI web page at http://www.ddialliance.org/controlled-vocabularies

universe.bestPracticeDefinition: Description of the population covered by the data in the file; the group of people or other elements that are the object of the study and to which the study results refer. Age, nationality, and residence commonly help to delineate a given universe, but any number of other factors may be used, such as age limits, sex, marital status, race, ethnic group, nationality, income, veteran status, criminal convictions, and more. The universe may consist of elements other than persons, such as housing units, court cases, deaths, countries, and so on. In general, it should be possible to tell from the description of the universe whether a given individual or element is a member of the population under study. Also known as the universe of interest, population of interest, and target population.
universe.example:
• Canadians aged 12-30 (Source:https://doi.org/10.5683/SP/HY2H1A)
• Queen's University 2nd year medical students who were part of the 2016 Critical Enquiry Course in the School of Medicine and agreed to participate in the study.(Source:https://doi.org/10.5683/SP/D6NISS)

timeMethod.bestPracticeDefinition: The time method or time dimension of the data collection, such as panel, cross-sectional, trend, time-series, or other.

dataCollector.bestPracticeDefinition: Individual, agency or organization responsible for administering the questionnaire or interview or compiling the data.
dataCollector.example: Trained student interviewers, both anglophone and francophone. (Source:https://hdl.handle.net/10864/ZJ17A)

collectorTraining.bestPracticeDefinition: Type of training provided to the data collector
collectorTraining.example:
• The interviews were conducted by professional interviewers under the supervision of the Institute for Social Science Research. (Source: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/SRVIO4)
• From the documentation: "Each staff member was thoroughly trained prior to beginning work on the survey. Interviewers received about three days of classroom training plus self-training materials. Additional study materials and classroom training were planned throughout the interviewing period. Quality control measures, such as editing returns, observing interviews and re-interviewing selected households were employed throughout the survey.” (Source: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/YT09KD)

frequencyOfDataCollection.bestPracticeDefinition: If the data collected includes more than one point in time, indicate the frequency with which the data was collected; that is, monthly, quarterly, or other.
frequencyOfDataCollection.example:
• Annual
• Hourly
• Data was collected at baseline and at one month follow-up. (Source:https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10889)

samplingProcedure.bestPracticeDefinition: Type of sample and sample design used to select the survey respondents to represent the population. May include reference to the target sample size and the sampling fraction.
samplingProcedure.example:
• Canadian adults randomly selected from Angus Reid Forum panel members. (Source:https://hdl.handle.net/10864/11510)
• Probability (Source: https://ddialliance.org/Specification/DDI-CV/SamplingProcedure_1.1.html)

targetSampleActualSize.bestPracticeDefinition:
Actual sample size.
Tip: The research study’s actual sample size may be stated in this numeric field for reference purposes.

targetSampleSizeFormula.bestPracticeDefinition:
Formula used to determine target sample size.
Tip: A plain-text, general description of a sample size formula may be stated here for reference purposes. This may include particular methodologies, practices, and outcomes from existing scholarly literature.
targetSampleSizeFormula.example: Eligible employees who lived within the following FSAs: K6V, K7A, K7C, K7G, K7H, K7K, K7L, K7M, K7N, K7P, K7R, K8N, K8P, K8R, K8V, K0E, K0G, K0H, K0K.

deviationsFromSampleDesign.bestPracticeDefinition: Show correspondence as well as discrepancies between the sampled units (obtained) and available statistics for the population (age, sex-ratio, marital status, etc.) as a whole.
deviationsFromSampleDesign.example:
• The suitability of Ohio as a research site reflected its similarity to the United States as a whole. The evidence extended by Tuchfarber (1988) shows that Ohio is representative of the United States in several ways: percent urban and rural, percent of the population that is African American, median age, per capita income, percent living below the poverty level, and unemployment rate. Although results generated from an Ohio sample are not empirically generalizable to the United States, they may be suggestiveof what might be expected nationally.(Source: https://ddialliance.org/Specification/DDI-Codebook/2.5/XMLSchema/field_level_documentation_files/schemas/codebook_xsd/elements/deviat.html)
• Oversample of persons 50 and older (Source: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/FGTJGO)

collectionMode.bestPracticeDefinition: Method used to collect the data; instrumentation characteristics (e.g., telephone interview, mail questionnaire, or other).
collectionMode.example:
• Interview
• Paper and online questionnaire
• Coded from psychiatric hospital files, court records, and police agencies. (Source:https://hdl.handle.net/10864/12053)

researchInstrument.bestPracticeDefinition: Type of data collection instrument used. Structured indicates an instrument in which all respondents are asked the same questions/tests, possibly with precoded answers. If a small portion of such a questionnaire includes open-ended questions, provide appropriate comments. Semi-structured indicates that the research instrument contains mainly open-ended questions. Unstructured indicates that in-depth interviews were conducted.
researchInstrument.example:
• Questionnaire
• Structured
• Technical instrument: Static Chamber, Vaisala Humicap HM70 relative humidity/ temperature probe, Vaisala Carbocap GMP343 infrared analyzer, Hobo Pro v2 U23-003 temperature logger, Kestrel 3500 weather meter, Taylor 9878 thermometer. (Source:https://hdl.handle.net/10864/12053)

dataCollectionSituation.bestPracticeDefinition: Description of noteworthy aspects of the data collection situation. Includes information on factors such as cooperativeness of respondents, duration of interviews, number of call backs, or similar.
dataCollectionSituation.example: There were 1,419 respondents who answered questions in telephone interviews lasting approximately 35 minutes each. Clarifications to survey questions were limited and respondents were directed to provide a response based on the information provided as to not allow interviewer bias/assumptions to influence the survey results.(Source:https://hdl.handle.net/10864/ZJ17A)

actionsToMinimizeLoss.bestPracticeDefinition: Summary of actions taken to minimize data loss. Include information on actions such as follow-up visits, supervisory checks, historical matching, estimation, and so on.
actionsToMinimizeLoss.example:
• Reminder e-mails were distributed to target population. (Source:https://doi.org/10.5683/SP/L1H3SS)
• Cards reminding parents about the follow-up visit were given out. (Source:https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10889)

controlOperations.bestPracticeDefinition: Methods to facilitate data control performed by the primary investigator or by the data archive.
controlOperations.example:
• Field validation is built into REDCap data collection forms. (Source: https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10907)
• Blinded double data entry and third person cross-validation were used. (Source: https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10900)

weighting.bestPracticeDefinition: The use of sampling procedures might make it necessary to apply weights to produce accurate statistical results. Describes the criteria for using weights in analysis of a collection. If a weighting formula or coefficient was developed, the formula is provided, its elements are defined, and it is indicated how the formula was applied to the data.
weighting.example:
• Rim weighting is used with this file. By region, the file was weighted to census targets on sex (wtsex), age (Wtage), and education (Wtedu) using the 2011 census. For this file, a religion weight (wtreligion) was also included based on the 2011 National Household Survey (NHS). The wtg2 variable includes all of these weights within it. (Source: https://doi.org/10.5683/SP/78RONJ)
• The final sample obtained for each area is not proportional to the Alberta population it makes up. For instance, Edmonton is over-sampled as shown by TABLE 1. Edmonton makes up only 24% of the Alberta population but has 43% of the interviews. Therefore, inorder to combine the samples for a provincial sample weighting is necessary. The weighting factors used for the 1987 survey are as follows: Edmonton 0.558439, Calgary 1.151521, and Other Alberta 1.471173. (Source: https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10567)
• wtx used to correctly weight respondents against Stats Canada Alberta population estimates (Source: https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10813)

cleaningOperations.bestPracticeDefinition: Methods used to clean the data collection, such as consistency checking, wildcode checking, or other.
cleaningOperations.example:
• For income data, all respondents are matched to the tax data file unless they refuse to have their information linked. Data obtained from the tax file are complete and do not require imputation. Income figures are imputed only in the absence of tax data. Donor imputation by the nearest neighbour method is generally used and is performed primarily with Statistics Canada’s Census Edit and Imputation System (CANCEIS). However, amounts received through certain government programs such as the universal childcarebenefit and child tax benefits are derived from other information (e.g.,number of children in the household) using a deductive imputation method. (Source: http://hdl.handle.net/11272/10619)
• Physiological data was reviewed for outliers. Individual breaths with tidal volume (VT), respiratory rate (RR) or minute ventilation (VE) that lay outside the 95% confidence interval for all infants were removed as outliers; 99.7% of all measured breaths were included in the final analyses. (Source: https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10910)

datasetLevelErrorNotes.bestPracticeDefinition: Note element used for any information annotating or clarifying the methodology and processing of the study.
datasetLevelErrorNotes.example: The computerized questionnaire contains many features designed to maximize the quality of the data collected. Many edits are built into the questionnaire to compare the reported data with unusual values and detect logical inconsistencies. When an edit fails, the interviewer is prompted to correct the information (with the respondent’s help, if necessary). Once the data are transmitted to Head Office, a comprehensive series of processing steps are undertaken for the purpose of detailed verification of each questionnaire. Invalid responses are corrected or flagged for imputation. Edits were applied at a micro level. Deterministic edits and consistency edits were also performed at the micro level. Data was checked for outliers and extreme values andwere corrected at a micro level when required. (Source: http://hdl.handle.net/11272/10619)

responseRate.bestPracticeDefinition: Percentage of sample members who provided information.
responseRate.example:
• Based on 100km radius, the survey response rate is 1874/3994 (46.9%), and the survey completion rate is 1732/3994 (43.4%). Based on FSAs for locations served by Kingston Transit, the survey response rate is 1469/3151 (46.6%), and the survey completion rate is 1356/3151 (43.0%). (Source: https://doi.org/10.5683/SP/CNXSVN)
• At one-month follow-up: 60.2% (n=136/226). (Source: https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10889)

samplingErrorEstimates.bestPracticeDefinition: Measure of how precisely one can estimate a population value from a given sample.Tip: Examples include confidence intervals, non-response, response bias.
samplingErrorEstimates.example:
• In SFS 2016, the 95% confidence interval for the average net worth of Canadian families had a width of $38,500. (Source: http://hdl.handle.net/11272/10619)
• + or -2.5%; design effect of weighting not calculated (Source: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/FGTJGO)

otherDataAppraisal.bestPracticeDefinition: Other issues pertaining to the data appraisal. Describe issues such as response variance, nonresponse rate and testing for bias, interviewer and response bias, confidence levels, question bias, or similar.
otherDataAppraisal.example: OSBD is subject to interpretation since it is an indirect behavioral measure of perceived distress. (Source: https://doi.org/10.7939/DVN/10841)

socialScienceNotesText.example: Info (Misc) v2 note: Corrections were made to variables: PAS1MRG1, PAS1MRG2, PASRDPO1, PASRDPO2, PASRDPO3, PASRDPO4, PASRDPO5 and VERDATE. (Source: http://hdl.handle.net/11272/10619)

astroType.bestPracticeDefinition:
The nature or genre of the content of the files in the dataset.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that
apply. Most of the types originate in the Virtual
Observatory (VO) Discovery and Provenance
Metadata46 specification. For type definitions, see the
table below.

astroFacility.bestPracticeDefinition:
The observatory or facility where the data was obtained.
Tip: For theoretical data, identify the computational
facility where it was obtained. Repeat the element
when naming more than one facility.

astroInstrument.bestPracticeDefinition:
The instrument used to collect the data.
Tip: Identify a specific instrument or an instrument
type for observational data. Provide the name of the
computer code for theoretical data.

astroObject.bestPracticeDefinition:
Astronomical Objects represented in the data (Given as SIMBAD recognizable names preferred).
Note: The SIMBAD database47 provides a concordance
for different name schemes. For the non-specialist, it
is somewhat difficult to use.

resolution.Spatial.bestPracticeDefinition:
The spatial (angular) resolution that is typical of the observations, in decimal degrees.
Tip: The spectral resolution may also be given as the
difference between velocities Δ v, calculated by using
the Doppler effect, that can be distinguished in a line
of the spectrum.

resolution.Spectral.bestPracticeDefinition: The spectral resolution that is typical of the observations, given as the ratio \u03bb/\u0394\u03bb.
resolution.Spectral.example:
5000
Given here as λ/Δλ
0.15 km/s
Given here as Δ v

resolution.Temporal.bestPracticeDefinition: The temporal resolution that is typical of the observations, given in seconds.

coverage.Spectral.Bandpass.bestPracticeDefinition:
Conventional bandpass name
Tip: Specific bandpass names include: optical
bandpasses (U, V, B, R, I); and narrow line filters (H-
alpha, [OIII]).
coverage.Spectral.Bandpass.example:
u’, g’, r’, i’, z’
U, B, V, JHK, 450

coverage.Spectral.CentralWavelength.bestPracticeDefinition:
The central wavelength of the spectral bandpass, in meters.
Note: This is not an IVOA-RM element.

coverage.Spectral.MinimumWavelength.bestPracticeDefinition: The minimum wavelength of the spectral bandpass, in meters.

coverage.Spectral.MaximumWavelength.bestPracticeDefinition: The maximum wavelength of the spectral bandpass, in meters.

coverage.Temporal.StartTime.bestPracticeDefinition:
Dataset Start Date
Tip: Provide a date or date/time (preferred) in ISO
8601 format
(e.g., YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).

coverage.Temporal.StopTime.bestPracticeDefinition:
Dataset End Date
Tip: Provide a date or date/time (preferred) in ISO
8601 format
(e.g., YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).

coverage.Spatial.bestPracticeDefinition:
The sky coverage of the data object.
Note: Follow the syntax found in the Space-Time
Coordinate (STC) Metadata Recommendation.
coverage.Spatial.example:
PositionInterval FK5 145.17 –
1.25 235.9 1.25
PositionInterval FK5 250.71
52.15 267.0 66.29
PositionInterval FK5 350.43 –
1.25 359.99 1.17
PositionInterval 0.0 –1.25
56.37 1.17

coverage.Depth.bestPracticeDefinition:
The (typical) depth coverage, or sensitivity, of the data object in Jy.
Tip: This is the faintest flux of energy that can be
perceived (units: Jensky (Jy)).

coverage.ObjectDensity.bestPracticeDefinition:
The (typical) density of objects, catalog entries, telescope pointings, etc., on the sky, in number per square degree.
Tip: Objects could be stars, galaxies, planets, star
clusters, asteroids, etc.

coverage.ObjectCount.bestPracticeDefinition:
The total number of objects, catalog entries, etc., in the data object.
Tip: Objects could be stars, galaxies, planets, star
clusters, asteroids, etc.

coverage.SkyFraction.bestPracticeDefinition: The fraction of the sky represented in the observations, ranging from 0 to 1.

redshiftType.bestPracticeDefinition:
RedshiftType string C "Redshift"; or "Optical" or "Radio" definitions of Doppler velocity used in the data object.
Note: This is not an IVOA-RM element. Tip: The light coming from an object moving away from you is redshifted (Doppler effect), which means that the frequency of that light is shifted to a lower value. The speed of an object can be computed by measuring the shifts in frequencies of peaks in its spectra. Since the Universe is expanding, the more distant an object is, the more it is redshifted. For that reason, redshift is used as a unit of distance for the most distant objects. This field RedshiftType serves to indicate which part of the spectra was used to measure the redshift.

resolution.Redshift.bestPracticeDefinition:
The resolution in redshift (unitless) or Doppler velocity (km/s) in the data object.
Note: This is not an IVOA-RM element.

coverage.Redshift.MinimumValue.bestPracticeDefinition:
The minimum value of the redshift (unitless) or Doppler velocity (km/s in the data object.
Note: This is not an IVOA-RM element.

coverage.Redshift.MaximumValue.bestPracticeDefinition:
The maximum value of the redshift (unitless) or Doppler velocity (km/s in the data object.
Note: This is not an IVOA-RM element.

studyDesignType.bestPracticeDefinition:
Design types that are based on the overall experimental design.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply. If there is no appropriate option, select Other and use the Other Design Type field.
studyDesignType.example:
●Case control
● Randomized controlled
trial
● Technological design

studyOtherDesignType.bestPracticeDefinition: If Other was selected in Design Type, list any other design types that were used in this Dataset.

studyFactorType.bestPracticeDefinition:
Factors used in the Dataset.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply. If there is no appropriate option, select Other and use the Other Factor Type field.

studyOtherFactorType.bestPracticeDefinition: If Other was selected in Factor Type, list any other factor types that were used in this Dataset.

studyAssayOrganism.bestPracticeDefinition:
The taxonomic name of the organism used in the Dataset or from which the starting biological material derives.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply. If there is no appropriate option, select Other and use the Other Organism field.
studyAssayOrganism.example:
● Homo sapiens
● Mus musculus
● Oryza sativa

studyAssayOtherOrganism.bestPracticeDefinition: If Other was selected in Organism, list any other organisms that were used in this Dataset. Terms from the NCBI Taxonomy are recommended.

studyAssayMeasurementType.bestPracticeDefinition:
A term to qualify the endpoint, or what is being measured (e.g. gene expression profiling; protein identification).
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply. If there is no appropriate option, select Other and use the Other Measurement Type field.

studyAssayOtherMeasurmentType.bestPracticeDefinition:
If Other was selected in Measurement Type, list any other measurement types that were used. Terms from NCBO Bioportal are recommended.
Tip: NCBO Bioportal is a searchable registry of hundreds of ontologies. Users can select an ontology and download the most recent version to see terms. New users may wish to either seek further guidance or disregard this recommended registry.

studyAssayTechnologyType.bestPracticeDefinition: A term to identify the technology used to perform the measurement (e.g. DNA microarray; mass spectrometry).
studyAssayTechnologyType.example:
● DNA microarray
● Flow cytometry
● Gel electrophoresis

studyAssayOtherTechnologyType.bestPracticeDefinition: If Other was selected in Technology Type, list any other technology types that were used in this Dataset.

studyAssayPlatform.bestPracticeDefinition: The manufacturer and name of the technology platform used in the assay (e.g. Bruker AVANCE).
studyAssayPlatform.example:
● Affymetrix
● AQI Biosciences
● BD BACTEC MGIT 320

studyAssayOtherPlatform.bestPracticeDefinition: If Other was selected in Technology Platform, list any other technology platforms that were used in this Dataset.

studyAssayCellType.bestPracticeDefinition: The name of the cell line from which the source or sample derives.
studyAssayCellType.example:
● Collar cell
● Scleral cell
● Unimodal nocireceptor

journalVolume.bestPracticeDefinition: The journal volume which this Dataset is associated with (e.g., Volume 4).

journalIssue.bestPracticeDefinition: The journal issue number which this Dataset is associated with (e.g., Number 2, Autumn).

journalPubDate.bestPracticeDefinition: The publication date for this journal volume/issue, which this Dataset is associated with (e.g., 1999).

journalArticleType.bestPracticeDefinition: Indicates what kind of article this is, for example, a research article, a commentary, a book or product review, a case report, a calendar, etc (based on JATS).

workflowType.bestPracticeDefinition: The kind of Computational Workflow, which is designed to compose and execute a series of computational or data manipulation steps in a scientific application

workflowCodeRepository.bestPracticeDefinition: A link to the repository where the un-compiled, human readable code and related code is located (e.g. GitHub, GitLab, SVN)

workflowDocumentation.bestPracticeDefinition: A link (URL) to the documentation or text describing the Computational Workflow and its use
